title: Erdős 269 running-LCM coordinates: prefix witnesses, jump channels, finite fibres, shells, and residue escape

concepts.label: three-prime running-LCM coordinates
concepts.note: Smooth lattice values, logarithmic height, reciprocal kernel, actual prefix, and literal prefix LCM.

concepts.label: extremal prefix witnesses
concepts.note: Divisibility of every prefix value into the height and occurrence of each maximal pure-power component.

concepts.label: three-prime logarithmic cell
concepts.note: Equality of all three integer-logarithm coordinates between two cutoffs.

concepts.label: finite pure-power jump channels
concepts.note: The positive prime-power channels, their disjoint union, and the unique common origin.

concepts.label: finite height-fibre coordinates
concepts.note: A finite exponent box partitioned by the actual running-LCM height of each lattice point.

concepts.label: variable-base tail step
concepts.note: The one-step integer orbit coordinate base*(state-digit).

concepts.label: filtered smooth exponent shell
concepts.note: Exponent triples in a bounded box whose smooth values lie in a half-open interval.

concepts.label: sorted quadratic budget
concepts.note: The denominator-free arithmetic inequality underlying the quadratic shell multiplicity bound.

concepts.label: residue escape window
concepts.note: A canonical positive residue lying above a proposed state bound and at most the modulus.

concepts.label: three-prime authority boundary
concepts.note: These declarations provide finite coordinates and elementary receipts only; the three-prime irrationality problem, rationality-to-carry identification, infinite ordering, and cofinal escape producer remain open.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The three-prime coordinate system consists of smooth3Val p q r i j k = p^i q^j r^k, the logarithmic height p^(log_p x) q^(log_q x) r^(log_r x), its reciprocal rational kernel at a smooth lattice point, the logarithmically bounded and cutoff-filtered exponent prefix, and the literal LCM of that prefix. Every value in the actual prefix divides the height, and for x nonzero each of the three maximal pure-power components occurs in the prefix.
statement_nodes.engine: Exact definitions, logarithmic exponent bounds for each filtered prefix point, and Nat.pow_log_le_self for the three pure-power witnesses.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The coordinate system is the finite three-prime restriction of the classical prime-power description of an LCM; no novelty claim is made.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: This node records the coordinates and the two divisibility directions' local witnesses, not the already-authored equality theorem itself. It proves no infinite reindexing, convergence, irrationality, or transcendence statement.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: SameThreePrimeLogCell p q r x y means exactly that log_p x=log_p y, log_q x=log_q y, and log_r x=log_r y.
statement_nodes.engine: Exact conjunction of the three integer-logarithm coordinate equalities.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Elementary cell coordinate for a piecewise-constant product of pure powers.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The definition alone states no constancy theorem and no ordering of cells. The height, LCM, and kernel constancy theorems remain separately authored in Z17.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For a prime p, positivePrimePowers p count is the image of exponents 1 through count under e↦p^e, so it excludes 1. Positive-power channels of two distinct primes are disjoint. threePrimePositiveJumpSet is the union of the first count positive powers in the p, q, and r channels, and threePrimeJumpSetWithOrigin adjoins the single common origin 1.
statement_nodes.engine: Finite-set images of positive exponents and uniqueness of powers of distinct prime bases.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Finite unique-factorisation bookkeeping for three prime-power channels.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: This is a finite jump-coordinate system. It neither orders the union, passes to all powers, nor proves any statement about the infinite running-LCM series; the already-authored cardinality theorems remain in Z17.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: smoothExponentBox hp hq hr is the rectangular box 0≤i≤hp, 0≤j≤hq, 0≤k≤hr. smoothPointHeight maps a triple to the three-prime height of its smooth value, and smoothHeightFiber p q r hp hq hr H filters the box to the triples whose point height is exactly H.
statement_nodes.engine: Finite rectangular product and exact filtering by the running-height map.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Standard finite fibre coordinates for regrouping a finite sum.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: These definitions form a finite full-box coordinate system, not the cutoff-filtered prefix and not an infinite series. They do not establish the already-authored fibre-sum normal form by themselves.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: tailStateStep base digit state is the integer base*(state-digit), the one-step coordinate used for the variable-base tail orbit.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: No orbit is constructed or analysed here, and this definition is not identified with the actual #269 rational tail. The rationality-to-carry instantiation remains open.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: smoothExponentShell p q r lo hi hp hq hr is the finite exponent box with bounds hp,hq,hr filtered to the triples whose smooth values lie in the half-open interval [lo,hi).
statement_nodes.engine: Finite rectangular exponent ranges and an exact lower-and-upper interval filter on smooth3Val.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The definition supplies no cardinality or tail estimate. Its bases and coordinate bounds are ordered parameters; the shell is not invariant under silently relabelling them.

statement_nodes.engine: From a≤b≤c derive a+2b≤j; with b=a+d, the remaining gap is the nonnegative product d(3a+4d+3).
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Elementary arithmetic-geometric comparison for three sorted coordinates.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: Sorting is a theorem hypothesis, not a free relabelling of an asymmetric smooth shell. This arithmetic inequality alone neither bounds a shell nor estimates an infinite tail.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: ResidueEscapesWindow C bound residue means exactly bound<residue≤C: the proposed residue lies strictly above the bounded-state window while remaining in the canonical positive residue range through the modulus.
statement_nodes.engine: Exact conjunction of strict escape above the bound and membership in the positive residue interval ending at C.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Elementary modular-window predicate used by the finite contradiction.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The predicate does not produce an escaping residue. The denominator-dependent cofinal local-window escape theorem and the identification of the actual rational tail with a bounded carry remain open.

intra_zone_relations.basis: The cell predicate freezes exactly the three logarithmic coordinates used by threePrimeHeight and therefore by the reciprocal kernel coordinate.
The prefix coordinates describe the running value at a cutoff; the channel coordinates describe the finite set of pure-power events at which those logarithmic maxima can change.
The point-height and fibre definitions apply the same smooth-value and logarithmic-height coordinates to a finite rectangular exponent domain.
Log cells explain why several lattice points can share a height, while fibres collect all points with one attained height without asserting that each fibre is a single cell.
Both are finite exponent-box filters: fibres filter by exact running height, whereas shells filter smooth values by a half-open multiplicative interval.
The arithmetic inequality supplies the denominator-free final budget used after a short shell has been injected into its two smallest coordinate ranges.
The affine step is the local recurrence coordinate, while the escape predicate is the finite modular condition consumed only after a bounded actual carry and an accumulated window have been supplied.
